I got stuck on the word "unit" in our LaneHelm rate-sheet notes. Until then, I was mostly checking whether the column headings lined up. Same heading, though, can hide a lot.

Two rates might both be in CAD and cover the same dates. One can still be per kilogram while the other is per shipment, and the math looks fine right up until the prices stop describing the same job.

The check I want beside the number is plain: what does this charge apply to? If I were on a Canadian freight team working from Excel, I'd verify that in the original customer and carrier sheets before trusting the comparison.

LaneHelm compares the rates saved in your workspace. A saved column connection can be reused when the next file has the same headers in the same order, but the new values and terms still need a look. That's the distinction I want our explanation to make clear.

Which rate unit makes you pause before preparing a quote?

#FreightQuoting #CanadianLogistics #RateManagement
